evidenceNotes: The predecessor HANDOFF_NOW state was validated as closing-environment-only and was not inherited as this environment's decision.

Live main and PR #129 predecessor facts were independently reverified before Stage 4 mutation: main df3fe061c7df3c4235aa2394623e703a4412ca46, sealed Stage 3 head e3f462306e1d2b0822aaf54eb1f9dc9af62ed4f8, all 14 exact-head workflow families successful, zero submitted reviews and zero inline review threads.
Stage 4 uses only the already-reserved rivalries/{rivalryId}/state/authoritative and nested idempotency path; sessions remain outside the implementation boundary.
A direct exact-rivalry browser pointer is stored only in IndexedDB convenience metadata; there is no account-wide rivalry listing or public discovery route.
The deterministic remote shared save identity is the creator slot's stable saveId while each paired slot retains its own local saveId linkage in rivalry governance metadata.

The client builds an immutable mutation plan before provider retries, binds state to a SHA-256 idempotency-key hash and request fingerprint, and rejects stale revisions or tombstones without rebasing.

Firestore Rules cross-check state.data.mutationReceipt against the exact getAfter idempotency receipt in the same transaction, preventing a browser from opening shared-state authority without the paired mutation receipt.

The Stage 4 emulator matrix covers two-account create/update, exact replay, reused-key conflict, stale CAS, third-account denial, required-account disable freeze, device revocation, tombstone anti-resurrection and session-write denial.
The permanent validation topology remains 14 workflow families because Stage 4 was added to the existing private-pairing workflow rather than creating a new workflow file.

Package-lock reconstruction briefly changed three dependency integrity strings; the exact unintended deltas were identified and restored, and a compare against the pre-edit commit verified that only the two intended version fields remain changed.

Pre-PR source audit found productionFirebaseRuntime browserFirestoreWrites/writeScope still labeled self-account-create-only even though Stage 3 production pairing and Stage 4 candidate writes use the same browser Firestore service. The shared runtime scope is now explicitly spark-private-account-device-pairing-connected-rivalry-state while the Connected Account controller itself remains self-account-create-only.

Pre-PR source audit found Connected Rivalry independently loaded at startup could race the intentionally lazy Connected Account and Private Pairing modules. The independent app.js load was removed and sparkConnectedAccount now loads Connected Rivalry only after the Private Pairing module is mounted.
